### تعبير الشباب: شواهد لإثراء حصيلتك التعبيرية

#### الشباب

قال تعالى: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ فِتْيَةٌ آمَنُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى﴾.

قال (ﷺ): «سَبْعَةٌ يُظِلُّهُمُ اللهُ فِي ظِلِّهِ يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ... شَابٌ نَشَأَ فِي طَاعَةِ اللهِ...» (متفق عليه).

قال الشاعر:

إِذَا أَنَا أَكْبَرْتُ شَأْنَ الشَّبَابِ .. فَإِنَّ الشَّبَابَ أَبُو الْمُعْجِزَاتِ

#### الأخلاق

قال تعالى: ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾.

قال (ﷺ): «إِنَّ أَقْرَبَكُمْ مِنِّي مَجْلِسًا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَحَاسِنُكُمْ أَخْلَاقًا» (رواه الترمذي).

قال (ﷺ): «إِنَّمَا بُعِثْتُ لِأُتَمِّمَ مَكَارِمَ الْأَخْلَاقِ».

قال الشاعر:

إِنَّمَا الْأُمَمُ الْأَخْلَاقُ مَا بَقِيَتْ .. فَإِنْ هُمُ ذَهَبَتْ أَخْلَاقُهُمْ ذَهَبُوا

#### حب الوطن (الوطن - الوطنية - الانتماء)

قال (ﷺ): «حُبُّ الْوَطَنِ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ» (رواه أحمد).

قال الشاعر:

وَطَنِي لَوْ شُغِلْتُ بِالْخُلْدِ عَنْهُ .. نَازَعَتْنِي إِلَيْهِ فِي الْخُلْدِ نَفْسِي

قال الشاعر:

لَوْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِصْرُ الْعَرِيقَةُ مَوْطِنِي .. لَعَرَسْتُ بَيْنَ تُرَابِهَا وَجْدَانِي

قال الشاعر:

وَلِي وَطَنٌ آلَيْتُ أَلَّا أَبِيعَهُ .. وَأَلَّا أَرَى غَيْرِي لَهُ الدَّهْرَ مَالِكَا

#### العلم والعمل

قال تعالى: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

قال تعالى: ﴿إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مَنْ أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا﴾.

قال (ﷺ): «مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَبْتَغِي فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَلَكَ اللهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ» (رواه مسلم).

قال (ﷺ): «إِنَّ اللهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلًا أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ» (رواه الطبراني).

قال الشاعر:

فِي ازْدِيَادِ الْعِلْمِ إِرْغَامُ الْعِدَا .. وَجَمَالُ الْعِلْمِ إِصْلَاحُ الْعَمَلِ

#### الصداقة

قال (ﷺ): «المَرْءُ عَلَى دِينِ خَلِيلِهِ فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَحَدُكُمْ مَنْ يُخَالِلُ» (رواه أبو داود).

قال الشاعر:

وَاحْذَرْ مُصَاحَبَةَ اللَّئِيمِ فَإِنَّهُ .. يُعْدِي كَمَا يُعْدِي الصَّحِيحَ الْأَجْرَبُ

قال الشاعر:

عَاشِرْ أُنَاسًا بِالذَّكَاءِ تَمَيَّزُوا .. وَاخْتَرْ صَدِيقَكَ مِنْ ذَوِي الْأَخْلَاقِ

<!-- بداية الصفحة 116 -->
### أهمية الماء
- قال تعالى: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾.
- قال الشاعر:

فَحَافِظٌ بُنَيَّ رَعَاكَ الْإِلَهُ **وَ لَوْ أَنَّ أَنْهَارَهُ جَارِيَهْ**

فَمَنْ يُهْدِرِ الْمَاءَ كَانَ جَزَاهُ **عَذَابًا عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الْجَانِيَهْ**

### الرياضة
- القول المأثور عن عمر بن الخطاب (رضي الله عنه): «عَلِّمُوا أَوْلَادَكُمُ السِّبَاحَةَ وَالرَّمَايَةَ وَرُكُوبَ الْخَيْلِ».
- قال الشاعر:

إِذَا مَا كُنْتَ ذَا جِسْمٍ سَلِيمٍ **فَإِنَّ الْعَقْلَ فِي الجِسْمِ السَّلِيمِ**

### القراءة
- قال تعالى: ﴿اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾.
- قال الشاعر:

أَنَا مَنْ بَدَّلَ بِالْكُتُبِ الصَّحَابَا **لَمْ أَجِدْ لِي وَافِيًا إِلَّا الْكِتَابَا**

- قال الشاعر:

أَعَزُّ مَكَانٍ فِي الدُّنَا سَرْجُ سَابِحٍ **وَخَيْرُ جَلِيسٍ فِي الزَّمَانِ كِتَابُ**

### النيل
- قال الشاعر:

مِيَاهُكَ كَالرُّوحِ تُحْيِي الْبِلَادَ **وَتَغْمُرُ بِالْخَيْرِ أَرْكَانَهَا**

تَهُنَّ الحُقُولَ عَلَى جَانِبَيْكَ **وَيَمْلَأُ فَيْضُكَ عُدْرَانَهَا**

### الوقت
- قال رسول الله (ﷺ): «لَا تَزُولُ قَدَمَا عَبْدٍ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حَتَّى يُسْأَلَ عَنْ أَرْبَعٍ: عَنْ عُمْرِهِ فِيمَا أَفْنَاهُ...» (رواه الترمذي).
- قال الشاعر:

دَقَّاتُ قَلْبِ الْمَرْءِ قَائِلَةٌ لَهُ **إِنَّ الحَيَاةَ دَقَائِقٌ وَثَوَانِي**

- قال الشاعر:

يَا مَنْ يُضَيِّعُ عُمْرَهُ **مُتَمَادِيًا فِي اللهْوِ أَمْسِكْ**

وَاعْلَمْ بِأَنَّكَ لَا مَحَالَةَ **ذَاهِبٌ كَذَهَابِ أَمْسِ**

### مكانة اللغة العربية
- قال تعالى: ﴿إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
- قال الشاعر على لسان اللغة العربية:

أَنَا الْبَحْرُ فِي أَحْشَائِهِ الدُّرُّ كَامِنٌ **فَهَلْ سَاءَلُوا الغَوَّاصَ عَنْ صَدَفَاتِي**

- قال الشاعر:

لُغَةَ الْقُرْآنِ يَا شَمْسَ الْهُدَى **صَانَكِ الرَّحْمَنُ مِنْ كَيْدِ الْعِدَى**

### نموذج تطبيقي للتعبير الإبداعي

#### المقال

«الأسرة الطيبة أصلها ثابتٌ تُؤتي ثمارها على أبنائها كل حين، وكم قرأنا في الكتب عن مفاهيم الرعاية والتربية! وها نحن نرى الأسر المصرية في معدنها وتصرفاتها من خير أُسَر العالم؛ فما زالت القيم الدينية تسيطر عليها، وما زالت الأسرة المصرية مترابطةً تربط بينها أواصر الرحمة والمودة والحب ورقابةِ الآباء والأمهات على أبنائهم، واحترام الأبناء لآبائهم وأمهاتهم، وتوقيرهم، وإجلالهم وطاعة أوامرهم، والأخذ بنصائحهم في أغلب الأمور.

أما الأحداث الفردية التي تقرؤها عن تهتُكِ صلاتِ الرحم فهي لا تدلُّ إِلَّا على الندرة؛ فإنَّ من الطبيعي والإيجابي أن الآباء والأمهاتِ هم من يرعون أبناءهم ويُحيطونهم ويبذلون في سبيلهم كلَّ مرٍّ تخص وغالٍ من مالٍ أو جهدٍ في سبيل تأمين حاضرهم ومستقبلهم، كما أنَّ الأبناء سيبادلون آباءهم وأمهاتهم فيبرونهم ويخفضون لهم جناحَ الذلِّ من الرحمةِ، ويقولون: ربنا ارحمهما كما ربياني صغارًا.

قال تعالى: ﴿إِنْ أَحْسَنتُمْ أَحْسَنتُمْ لِأَنفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا﴾، وقال تعالى: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾.

إن الهم الأكبر للوالدين هو سعادة أبنائهم - بنين وبنات - حتى بعد أن يكبروا، تلك هي الحياة التي لا يخرجُ عنها إلا القلةُ الضئيلة من أصحاب النفوس العليلة والقلوب الصلبة المتحجرة.

والشاعر يقول:

متى يبلغ البنيان يومًا كمالَهُ :: إذا كُنْتَ تَبنيه وغيرُك يهدِمُ؟

وختامًا، الأسرة مجتمع صغير كلما اهتمت برعاية وتربية أبنائها صَلُحَ المجتمع كله، وعاش الناسُ في أمن وأمان، وكان مستقبلنا خيرًا من ماضينا».

# القصة المقررة: أبو الفوارس عنترة بن شداد

## الفصل الأول: مُغنّي القافلة

### ملخص لأهم أحداث القصة

#### ملخص الفصل الأول (مُغنّي القافلة)

- كانت عبلة آتية في قافلة من عُرس ابنة خالتها في قبيلة هوازن إلى منازل قومها عبس في أرض الشرية والعلم السعدي.
- كان عنترة بن شداد العبسي يقود القافلة، وهو يتغنى بقصائد يمزج فيها بين أنغام الحرب وأنغام الغزل.
- وصلت القافلة إلى فم الوادي، فأناخ عنترة بعيره وأزاح الستار عن الهودج الذي فيه عبلة، وقال لها باسما: منزل كريم يا عبلة. وأنزلها من الهودج.
- أقبل نحو عبلة نساء أعمامها وبناتهن، فأسرعت نحوهن لتستقبلهن، وكانت فيهن ابنة عمها مروة ابنة شداد.
- فرق عنترة العبيد، فأمر بعضهم أن يسقوا الإبل، وأمر آخرين أن يقيموا خيام النساء، وأمر غيرهم أن يوقدوا النيران لإعداد الطعام.
- ركب عنترة حصانه، ودار حول الوادي؛ ليطمئن على المكان الذي نزلوا فيه.
- عاودت عنترة ذكريات أحلامه؛ إذ تذكَّر أنه عبد الشداد، ولا يجرؤ على أن يفوز من عبلة بأكثر من أن يدعوها قائلًا: سيدتي.
- كان عنترة يحاذر أن يتحدث أحد بأنه يتطلع إلى عبلة، فما كان أبوها مالك ليرضى أن يتطلع عبد مثله إلى ابنته، وكذلك أخوها عمرو لم يكن ليرضى أن يعيره أصحابه بذلك.
- امتلأ قلب عنترة حزنًا؛ فهو الذي يحمي حمى عبس، وهو الفارس الذي سار ذكره في قبائل العرب، ومع ذلك فقد كان لا يزيد على أن يكون عبدًا لشداد.
- طلبت الفتيات من عنترة أن ينشدهن الشعر، فرفض حتى تأذن له عبلة.
- أمرت عبلة عنترة بإنشاد الشعر، فأخذ يتغنى بشعره، وهو يمثل مواقفه في القتال ويصف فرسه في المعركة حتى انتهى إلى الغزل، فأخذ يصف محاسن محبوبته ونُبل شِيَمها وعُلُو حسبها، وتغيَّر مظهره فأصابته رجفة وتقطعت نبرات صوته، واتجه إلى عبلة كأنه يخاطبها بغزله.
- تعجبت الفتيات من شعر عنترة، ودهشت عبلة حيث كانت تلك أول مرة تسمعه ينشد فيها بهذه الحرارة.

## الفصل الثاني: البطل الثائر

- لم يكن هناك ما يدعو عنترة إلى الخوف من غارة مفاجئة؛ لأن القمر كان يقترب من التمام في شهر رجب، وما كان العرب لينتهكوا حرمة ذلك الشهر.
- سار عنترة يناجي نفسه، وقد شعر أنه أخطأ وأوضح عما يضمره في نفسه من حبه لعبلة.
- كان عنترة يتعجب من حاله، كيف يرضى أن يُقيم في قوم يدافع عنهم، ويحمل إليهم الغنائم، ثم لا يجد منهم إلَّا الإنكار والبخل.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 120 -->
## الفصل الثالث: الطريق إلى الحقيقة

عاد عنترة مع القافلة إلى حلة عبس، وكان يوم عودته موعد العيد السنوي للقبيلة.

ذهب عنترة إلى أمه زبيبة فاستقبلته فاتحة ذراعيها، ولكنه قابلها بجفاء وقسوة، وجلس غاضبًا.

سألته أمه عن سبب غضبه، فاتهمها بأنها السبب في شقائه وعبوديته.

ذكر عنترة أمه باليوم الذي جاءها فيه يبكي وهو صبي، شاكيًا أن قومه يعيرونه بها، فقالت له: لا تهتم بقولهم؛ فإنك ابن شداد.

أخبرت زبيبة عنترة بأنها ليست أَمَة؛ فهي الحُرة الحبشية (تانا) ابنة (ميجو) التي تدين بالمسيحية، وهي التي جاءت إلى هذه الأرض مخطوفة ومعها ابناها شيبوب وجرير. وقد هبط عليهم شداد وأنقذهم وأنجب منها عنترة.

قرر عنترة أن يذهب إلى شداد ويحدثه لعله يُلحقه بنسبه ويزيل عنه العار، ولكن زبيبة حذرته من هذا الأمر حتى لا يحدث بينه وبين أبيه صدام.

طمأنها عنترة بأنه سوف يخضع لأبيه في القول، ويتحدث معه برفق.

## الفصل الرابع: حوار ساخن

خرج عنترة من بيت أمه، وسار مسرعًا حتى بلغ البراح الفسيح الذي تحتفل فيه عبس بالعيد السنوي.

لم يكن عنترة يعرف سبب ذهابه، أهو صورة عبلة التي تجذبه؟ أم أن ضيق صدره يدفعه للهروب من الوحدة؟ أم أنه يرجو أن يلقى شداد بن قراد هناك؟

حيَّا عنترة الملك زهير بن جذيمة، ثم نظر إلى المكان فلم يجد به موضعًا للجلوس، وسمع صوت عمارة بن زیاد ساخرًا يقول له: ألا تجد لك مكانًا يا عنترة؟ فأجابه عنترة: لو أنصفت لقمت لي من مكانك يا عمارة. واصطدم الاثنان حتى هبَّ الملك من مكانه صائحًا: تريث يا عنترة، ويحك يا عنترة.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 121 -->
## الفصل الخامس: خطبة عبلة

- ذهب عنترة إلى الوادي الفسيح الذي كانت إبل شداد ترعى فيه، وكان هذا الوادي عزيزًا عليه حيث كان ملعبه وموضع لهوه وأسماره.
- قضى عنترة أيامه ولياليه هائمًا في النهار بين الشعاب، سابحًا في الليل بين الشجون، وهو في كل لحظة تمر به يزداد حقدًا على قومه الذين يحتقرونه، وعلى أبيه الذي يظلمه وينكره.
- سمع عنترة وقع حوافر فرس يأتي من ورائه مسرعًا، فذهب ليرى من يكون ذلك، فرأى أخاه شيبوبًا، وتوقع أنه آتٍ إليه بشيء خطير.
- أخبر شيبوب عنترة بأن عمارة بن زياد ذهب بالأمس إلى مالك بن قراد؛ ليخطب ابنته عبلة، فوقع الخبر على عنترة وقع الصاعقة، ووقف ينظر إلى الفضاء مبهوتًا.
- نصح شيبوب عنترة بأن يفكر في أمره بتعقل؛ لأنه يرى أن عنترة يخدع نفسه ويجري وراء سراب، فلن يرضى مالك به زوجًا لابنته.
- أخبر عنترة شيبوبًا بأنه رضي بالرق أول الأمر؛ لأنه كان قريبًا من عبلة، ورفضه بعد ذلك؛ لأنه يبعده عنها.
- عزم عنترة على أن يحارب قومه بسيفه انتصافًا لنفسه، وأن يحارب شدادًا إذا ضن عليه باسمه، وأن يحارب مالكًا إذا وقف بينه وبين حبه، وأن يحارب عمارة إذا تجرأ على أن يسلب حياته.

## الفصل السادس: البطل الحر

- عاد عنترة إلى عبس، وأوقد نار العداوة بينه وبين آل عمارة بن زياد.
- خرجت قبيلة عبس مع الملك زهير لغزو قبيلة طيئ، وتركوا في الحي طائفة قليلة لحراسة المنازل يقودها شداد بن قراد.
- رفض عنترة الخروج مع قومه تشفيًا منهم؛ لأنهم لا ينصفونه.
- لم يستطع عنترة أن يلقى عبلة؛ لأنها منذ خُطبت لعمارة ضُرِبَ عليها الحجاب بأمر من أبيها وأخيها قبل رحيلهم مع الجيش.
- كان عنترة واقفًا على ربوة يتغنى بشعره، وإذا به يرى خيلًا تُقبل نحو الوادي وتهجم على عبس، وحاول فوارس عبس أن يدافعوا عن قبيلتهم، ولكنهم كانوا قلة فلم يثبتوا أمام العدو.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 122 -->
## الفصل السابع: انتصار

- تحركت نفس عنترة إلى القتال مِرارًا، وهم أن يهبط من الربوة لينصر قومه، ولكنه غالب نفسه ومنعها.
- خُيّل لعنترة أن المعركة قد وصلت إلى قريب من دار عبلة، فاندفع نازلًا عن الربوة، ووثب على فرسه وهمزه متجهًا نحو ميدان المعركة.
- رأى عنترة أباه شدادًا مقبلًا عليه بفرسه، وطلب شداد منه أن يدافع عن قومه الذين يُصرَعون، ولكن عنترة رفض حتى يعترف به أبوه وقومه.
- اعترف شداد بعنترة ابنًا له، فوثب عنترة على فرسه وأسرع لقتال الأعداء.

- حطم الأعداء بيوت بني عبس، وداسوا فرسانهم، وحينما أحسوا ريح النصر هدءوا عن القتال، وأقبل بعضهم على سلب البيوت، وطارد بعضهم النساء والأطفال؛ لكي يأخذوهم أسرى، فقد كان أكبر همهم أن يأخذوا النساء ليكن لهم إماءً.
- أقبل عنترة نحو الشعب، فكان أول همه أن يرى بيت مالك فلمحه من وراء المعمعة خاليًا مُهدّمًا.
- انقض عنترة على الأعداء، فكان يضرب العدو حينًا بفرسه، ويطعنه حينًا برمحه، وتساقط الأعداء حتى سمع فرسان عبس صيحته فانضموا إليه حتى هزموا الأعداء.
- اتجه عنترة إلى وادي الجواء للبحث عن عبلة، فأخبرته مروة بأن عبلة قد اختطفت.
- اندفع عنترة بفرسه للبحث عن عبلة، وقابل شيبوبًا الذي كان متنكرًا في زي امرأة، وأخبر شيبوب عنترة بأن عبلة خطفها ثلاثة من فرسان طيئ وساروا بها، وعزموا على قضاء الليلة عند ماء الربابية ليريحوا أفراسهم، ويستريحوا من عناء المعركة.
- اتجه عنترة مسرعًا إلى ماء الربابية والتقى بالفرسان الثلاثة، وقتل أحدهم وفر الاثنان بعد إصابتهما وأنقذ عنترة عبلة.
- عاد عنترة بعبلة، وقضت عبس أيامًا في عيد متصل؛ إذ كانت نجاتها إحدى العجائب التي جرت المقادير بتدبيرها.

## الفصل الثامن: علاقة قلقة

- علم الملك زهير بخداع الطائيين له وهجومهم على حلة عبس في غيبته، فأسرع عائدًا يعترض طريقهم حتى يأخذ حقه منهم، ولكنه لم يلق أحدًا في الطريق؛ فقد اتبعوا طريقًا أخرى حتى لا يلاقوه.
- دهش الملك زهير عندما وصل إلى عبس؛ لأنه وجد قومه يستقبلونه بالتهنئة والبشرى، وكان شداد في مقدمتهم، وإلى يمينه ابنه عنترة.
- مضت أيام كانت فيها الأعياد متصلة، وكان عنترة فيها محل اهتمام الجميع؛ فلولاه لكانت عبلة أسيرة، ولما كانت في عبس بقية.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 123 -->
### ملخص لأهم أحداث القصة

لم يستطع مالك وابنه عمرو أن يتعرضا لعنترة إذا تحدث إلى عبلة، وكذلك لم يستطع عمارة أن يظهر غضبًا إذا رأى عبلة تجالس عنترة أو تسايره وتناجيه.

سار عنترة في ليلة مع عبلة إلى بيتها، ودار بينهما حديث حول خطبتها لعمارة، واتهمها عنترة بالمراوغة فتضجرت منه ومن حديثه.

تألم عنترة أثناء حديثه مع عبلة؛ لأنه رأى أنها لم يعجبها من كلامه إلّا شعره.

اتهم عنترة عبلة بأنها معجبة بعمارة؛ لأنها رضيت به زوجًا، كما أن أباها أعد له وليمة كبيرة، وكانت هي تخدم عمارة بنفسها وتحث الإماء على إكرامه.

وصف عنترة زواج عبلة من عمارة بذهاب الأمة إلى بيت سيدها، فردت عليه بحنق وقالت: "إنما الأمة غيري".

عدد عنترة عبلة بأنه سوف يبعث إليها ليلة زفافها برأس عمارة؛ ليكون هدية عُرسها.

أحس عنترة أنه أخطأ في حديثه مع عبلة، فطلب منها العفو، ولكنها ذهبت إلى بيتها باكية، فضاق صدره واتجه نحو الصحراء.

## Lessons 1 & 2: Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt — Moments That Shaped Us

<!-- بداية الصفحة 3 -->
### Definitions, Synonyms & Antonyms

#### 1. Definitions

**crossroads (n)** — a place where two or more roads meet; it can also mean an important meeting point for people or ideas — مُلْتَقَى طُرُق

**identity (n)** — the qualities, beliefs, history, and culture that make a person, group, or country different from others — هوية

**merchant (n)** — a person who buys and sells goods, especially as a job — تاجر

**neighborhood (n)** — areas of a town or city where people live — حي سكني - مجاورة

**preserve (v)** — to keep something safe and protect it from damage or loss — يحفظ - يُصُون

**pride (n)** — a feeling of happiness and respect because of something good or important — كبرياء - فخر

**proud (adj)** — feeling pleased and satisfied because of something good that you, your country, or someone else has done — فخور

**restore (v)** — to repair an old building, object, or place and make it look as it did before — يرمم - يعيد

**trade (n)** — the activity of buying, selling, or exchanging goods — تجارة

#### 2. Synonyms

| Word | Synonym (= Meaning) |
|------|---------------------|
| alive (adj) | living, breathing |
| carved (adj) | shaped, cut, engraved, sculpted |
| crossroads (n) | intersection, junction — ملتقى طرق - نقطة تقاطع |
| harmony (n) | coordination, agreement — تناغم - انسجام |
| heritage (n) | legacy, inheritance — تراث |
| identity (n) | character, individuality — هوية |
| inspire (v) | motivate, encourage, stimulate — يُلهم |
| monument (n) | memorial, statue — أثر (مفرد آثار) |
| neighborhood (n) | area, district — حي سكني - مجاورة |
| preserve (v) | protect, conserve, keep — يحفظ - يصون |
| pride (n) | satisfaction, dignity — كبرياء - فخر |
| restore (v) | repair, renovate — يرمم - يعيد |

<!-- بداية الصفحة 4 -->
### Antonyms

| Word | Antonym (= Opposite) |
|------|----------------------|
| awareness (n) | ignorance, unawareness |
| determination (n) | indecision, hesitation |
| harmony (n) | conflict, disagreement, confusion, disharmony |
| inspire (v) | discourage, deter |
| knowledge (n) | ignorance, illiteracy, misunderstanding, unawareness |

### Grammar: Expressing Preference and Time

#### Expressing Preference with "Would Rather/Sooner"

- **Subj. + would rather/sooner + inf.**  
  This structure is used to express a preference.  
  *Example:* I'd rather go shopping in the afternoon.

- **Subj. + would rather/sooner + فاعل مختلف عن الفاعل الأول + past simple**  
  When the subject of the second clause is different from the first subject, the past simple is used after "would rather/sooner".  
  *Example:* I'd rather you arrived on time. = You don't arrive on time.

#### Expressing Time with "It's (about/almost/high) Time"

- **It is + (about/almost/high) + time + subject + past simple**  
  This structure is used to say that something should be done now or soon.  
  *Example:* It is high time you returned home. = You are still out.

#### Using Past Perfect with "I wish / I'd rather / It's (about/almost) time"

- The past perfect is used instead of the past simple when there is a time expression referring to the past after "I wish / I'd rather / It's (about/almost) time".  
  *Example:* I'd rather she had arrived home earlier yesterday.

#### Important Notes

- If a verb comes directly after "would rather", it is in the infinitive without "to".  
  **would rather + inf. / (not + inf.)**

- The presence of a frequency adverb such as "always, usually, often" indicates the repetition of an event in a specific tense, not only in the present simple.

#### Transformation Rules

- **Subj. + used to + inf. ... = Subj. + no longer + (inf.) / (inf. + s/es/ies) ... = Subj. + don't/doesn't + inf. ... anymore/any longer.**  
  *Example:* He used to smoke. = He no longer smokes. = He doesn't smoke anymore.

- **Subj. + stopped + (inf. + ing) ...**  
  *Example:* He stopped smoking.

### Rewriting Sentences with Specific Expressions

#### Using "used to", "no longer", "anymore", and "stopped"

When we want to talk about past habits or states that are no longer true, we can use different expressions. Each of these expressions gives the same meaning but with a different structure.

- **"Used to"** + infinitive: We use this to describe a past habit or state that is now finished.
    - Example: He **used to play** in the street when he was young.

- **"No longer"**: This expression means "not anymore" and is used to show that a past action or state has ended. It is usually placed before the main verb.
    - Example: He **no longer plays** in the street.

- **"Anymore"**: This word is used at the end of a sentence to show that something has stopped.
    - Example: He doesn't play in the street **anymore**.

- **"Stopped"** + gerund (-ing form): We use this to indicate that an action has ceased.
    - Example: I **stopped borrowing** books from the library.

#### The Subjunctive Mood with Specific Expressions

If a sentence contains one of the following expressions, the verb in that clause must be in the **past simple** (second form of the verb):

- **wish, wishes, wished**
- **It is (high/about) time**
- **would rather / would sooner**
- **would prefer it if**

**Rule:** Subject + 2nd conjugation (past simple)

#### Examples:

1.  I wish I **knew** the answer.
2.  It's time Hamza **went** to the club.
3.  Isn't it high time we **depended** on ourselves?
4.  I'd rather you **didn't come** now. I'm busy.
5.  She'd prefer it if you **didn't ask** her personal questions. She cares about her privacy.

#### The Past Perfect with Specific Expressions

If a sentence contains a time adverb referring to the past (such as **yesterday**, **last week**), the verb following these expressions must be in the **past perfect**:

- **would rather / would sooner**
- **wish, wishes, wished**
- **It was (high/about) time**

**Rule:** Subject + **had / hadn't** + past participle (p.p.)

#### Example:

- I wish I **had studied** harder yesterday.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 18 -->
### Subjunctive Mood with Different Subjects

#### Would rather / Would sooner + Different Subject

When the subject of the sentence after **would rather** or **would sooner** is different from the subject before it, we use the past simple tense to refer to the present or future, and the past perfect tense to refer to the past.

**Structure:**
- Subject + would rather/sooner + (that) + different subject + past simple (present/future meaning)
- Subject + would rather/sooner + (that) + different subject + past perfect (past meaning)

**Examples:**
- I'd rather you left the office early yesterday. We had too much work. (past meaning — past perfect would also be correct: *had left*)
- She'd rather he were taller. (present meaning — past simple with *were* for all persons)

#### Wish / Wishes / Wished + Different Subject

When the subject of the clause after **wish** is different from the subject of the main clause, we use the past simple to express a present wish and the past perfect to express a past wish.

#### It is (high/about) time + Different Subject

The expression **It is (high/about) time** is followed by a different subject and the past simple tense.

#### Would prefer it if + Different Subject

The expression **would prefer it if** is followed by a different subject and the past simple tense.

#### Important Note

The subject of the clause after these expressions must be different from the subject before them.

### Uses of the Past Continuous

#### 1. Uses of the Past Continuous

The past continuous is used to express an action that was in progress at a specific time in the past.

**Example:**
- I was playing on the beach last Friday afternoon.

#### 2. While / As / When

Used to express two actions that were both in progress at the same time in the past:

**Structure:** Past continuous clause + Past continuous clause

**Examples:**
- While I was reading a story, Ali was watching TV.

#### 3. While / As / When / Just as

Used to express an action that was in progress in the past when another action happened:

**Structure:** Past simple clause + Past continuous clause

**Examples:**
- While he was playing a tennis match, he broke his arm.
- = He broke his arm while he was playing a tennis match.

#### 4. While + infinitive + ing

**Structure:** While + verb-ing + Past simple clause

**Examples:**
- While playing a tennis match, he broke his arm.
- (Not: While a tennis ...)

#### 5. During + noun / noun phrase

**Structure:** Past simple clause + During + noun / noun phrase

**Examples:**
- During a tennis match, he broke his arm.
- (Not: During watching ...)

#### 6. When

**Structure:** Past continuous clause + When + Past simple clause

**Examples:**
- When I arrived, Shahd was watching a cartoon.

#### 7. On + noun / (verb + ing)

**Structure:** Past simple clause / Past continuous clause + On + noun / (verb + ing)

**Examples:**
- On my arrival at my office, the secretary was checking emails.

#### 8. While + preposition + noun

**Examples:**
- While in Alexandria, I ate fish for lunch every day.

#### 9. While / On + being + past participle

Note the use of the passive voice in the following form:

**Examples:**
- While the food was being cooked, it smelled nice.
- = While / On being cooked, the food smelled nice.

In the previous example, we used (being cooked) and not (cooking) because the second clause begins with (the food), which is considered the object of the first clause.

### استخدام الماضي البسيط بدلاً من الماضي المستمر مع بعض الأفعال

- **الحالة العقلية (Mental state):** realise, understand, know, mean, think (= believe), imagine, recognize, remember, forget... etc.

كما أن (being) لا تُستخدم كفعل أساسي في الماضي المستمر:

### Reading Texts On Lesson 4

Pride is not something that appears in a single day. It grows slowly, like a tree, from strong roots of history, culture, and shared values. For Egyptians, these roots run deep and continue to give us strength. Our country is one of the oldest and greatest civilizations in the world, and its story continues to inspire not only Egyptians, but people everywhere. True pride is built through connection to the past and responsibility for the future.

In ancient times, Egypt was a leader in human progress and knowledge. Our ancestors built the mighty pyramids and the magnificent temples along the Nile - monuments that still amaze the world today. They developed writing systems, advanced mathematics, and important medical knowledge. These achievements were not only for Egypt; they became gifts to the entire world, proving the greatness and creativity of our people.

Their heritage shows that Egyptians have always worked with vision and determination. Egypt was also a center for culture and learning. Great authors, poets, and thinkers shared their ideas and recorded their knowledge in writing. Their works reflected the values, traditions, and beliefs of the Egyptian society and influenced people for generations. Through stories, wisdom, and art, Egypt became a place where culture was preserved and celebrated. This role, as a home for creativity and expression, gave our nation respect and admiration from other civilizations.

True pride begins when we understand our history, protect our culture, and work hard for the future. It is not only about what we have inherited, but also about what we create for the generations to come. When we honor our past, stay united, and build our tomorrow with determination, we stand exactly where pride begins.

### What is an essay?

An essay is a short piece of writing on a particular topic. It presents ideas in an organized way, with a clear introduction, body paragraphs, and a conclusion.

المقالُ هُوَ قِطْعَةٌ قَصِيرَةٌ مِنَ الكِتَابَةِ عَنْ مَوْضُوعٍ مُعَيَّنٍ، وهو يَعْرِضُ الأفكارَ بِطَرِيقَةٍ مُنَظَّمَةٍ، مَعَ مُقَدِّمَةٍ وَاضِحَةٍ، وَفَقَرَاتِ مَثْنَى، وَخَاتِمَةٍ.

### Main parts of an essay

An essay has three main parts: Introduction, Body Paragraphs, and Conclusion.

يَتَكَوَّنُ المَقَالُ مِن ثَلاثَةِ أَجزاءٍ رَئِيسِيَّةٍ هي: المُقَدِّمَة، فقرات الموضوع، والخاتمة.

#### Introduction: The opening paragraph

**Purpose**  
To introduce the topic, grab the reader's attention, and present the thesis statement (main idea).

تُقَدِّمُ المَوْضوعَ، وَتَجْذِبُ انتباهَ القارئ، وَتَطْرَحُ الجُمْلَةَ الأساسية (الفكرة الرئيسية).

### Writing in Points: How to Handle Multiple-Choice Questions in the Exam Paper

#### An Essay

1. An essay is a short piece of writing about a particular topic.
2. An essay presents ideas in an organized way.
3. An essay has three main parts: an introduction, body paragraphs, and a conclusion.
4. The introduction is the opening paragraph of an essay.
5. The introduction presents the topic and grabs the reader's attention.
6. The introduction includes a hook, background information, and a thesis statement.
7. A hook is an interesting fact, question, or quote at the beginning of an essay.
8. A thesis statement presents the main idea or argument of the essay.
9. The body paragraphs are the main part of an essay.
10. Body paragraphs explain and support the thesis with details, examples, and evidence.
11. Each body paragraph begins with a topic sentence.
12. A topic sentence presents the main idea of the paragraph.
13. Supporting details are facts, examples, or reasons that explain the topic sentence.
14. A closing sentence ends the paragraph and links it to the main topic.
15. The conclusion is the final paragraph of an essay.
16. The conclusion summarizes the main points and restates the thesis in new words.
17. A conclusion may end with a final thought, final insight, or call to action.

It was a difficult week for Sama. Her grades were slipping, and she felt overwhelmed by all her schoolwork. On Thursday afternoon, she sat by her window, staring at the grey sky that seemed to mirror her mood. She hadn't spoken to many people lately and felt isolated from her friends.

Then, there was a knock at the door. It was Mrs. Aya, the friendly neighbor who lived upstairs. She held a small basket covered with a clean white cloth, still warm from the oven. "I baked some fresh bread this morning," Mrs. Aya said warmly. "I thought you might like some."

The smell was irresistible, wrapping around Sama like a gentle hug. Sama smiled for the first time in days and invited her in for tea. They sat together, chatting about small things – school, plants, and Mrs. Aya's garden, while the soft sound of rain tapped on the window. Slowly, Sama felt her worries began to fade.

### Listening Text

My name is Ahmed, and I'm 17 years old. Last year, I joined a community tree-planting project in my village. At first, I only wanted to get volunteering hours for school. But what happened during the project truly transformed me.

We worked in teams to dig holes, plant saplings, and water them. It was hard work under the hot sun, but we laughed a lot and supported each other. That's when I learned the meaning of real teamwork - not just working together, but caring if someone was tired or needed water.

One day, an old farmer came to watch. He said, "I haven't seen green like this in 20 years." His words stayed in my mind. I realized we weren't just planting trees - we were making a difference to the environment and to people's lives.

After three months, I felt different. I had more confidence to speak up, and I cared more about my community. Volunteering taught me responsibility - those trees depend on us. I even started a recycling corner at school.

Now, I believe volunteering isn't only about helping others. It's also about personal growth. You give time, but you get so much more - skills, friends, and pride. I will continue volunteering because it has become a lifelong habit. And yes, it's meaningful. When you serve others, your heart grows bigger.

Before leaving, Mrs. Aya said, "Sometimes, the smallest kindness can make a big difference." Sama kept thinking about those words. She decided to help her younger cousin with homework that evening. Seeing her cousin's face light up filled her with optimism. She realized that kindness doesn't just make others feel better; it can change your own heart, too.

### Voluntary Work

Voluntary work is an important part of building stronger communities and better societies. Unlike paid employment, voluntary work is done freely, without expecting financial rewards. People of all ages can participate, from young students to retired professionals, and their contributions make a visible difference in the lives of others.

One of the main values of voluntary work is that it teaches responsibility. When a person gives time to help others, they learn that their actions matter. For example, students who volunteer in hospitals or schools develop empathy and patience. They realize that even simple tasks, like reading stories to children or assisting elderly patients, bring joy and comfort. Everyone has to remember that helping others is essential.

Voluntary work also strengthens social connections. People from different backgrounds meet. They must cooperate and share experiences. This cooperation builds understanding and respect across cultures. Moreover, volunteering often gives individuals practical skills such as teamwork, problem-solving, and leadership, which later help them in professional life.

Finally, voluntary work is a source of personal satisfaction so we all should participate in it. Knowing that one's efforts have supported others creates pride and motivation. It proves that true wealth is not only measured in money, but also in kindness and service.

### Reading Text on Lesson 4 (SB page 32)

My name is Radwan, and I work as a firefighter in Alexandria. Many people think our job is just putting out fires, but it's much more than that. We rescue people from car accidents, help during floods, and sometimes save animals trapped in dangerous places.

The truth is, our work can be risky. I have entered burning buildings where smoke made it hard to see and breathe. I've stood on shaking ladders in the middle of the night, with the heat almost burning my skin. Sadly, I have also seen lives lost before we could reach them. These moments stay with me forever.

Yet, we do it because we believe in obligation - the duty to help each other, no matter the cost. In every emergency, we must act quickly, stay calm, and trust our training. We don't think about fear in those moments; we think about the people waiting for us.

I am proud to serve my community. I know that my work saves lives, and that is worth every risk. When you help others, you are not just doing a job; you are protecting hope itself.

### A Descriptive Essay

A descriptive essay is a piece of writing that uses words to create a picture for the reader. It is like painting a picture with words instead of paint. You can describe a person, place, object, or experience in a descriptive essay. The aim is to make the reader feel as if they are there.

A descriptive essay consists of an introduction, body paragraphs, and a conclusion. In the introduction, you introduce the person, place, or thing you will describe. You also give a general idea of why the topic is important to you.

The body usually consists of two or more paragraphs. Each body paragraph should focus on a different aspect or sense. One paragraph may describe what you see, while another describes what you hear or smell.

In the conclusion, you summarize the main ideas. The conclusion also presents your overall feeling about the topic.

A descriptive essay uses the five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. It gives many specific, clear, and vivid details. It creates a clear picture in the reader's mind. A descriptive essay usually focuses on one main person, place, thing, or feeling.

To write a good descriptive essay, use detailed words that help the reader see, hear, smell, taste, or feel what you describe.

### Reading Text - Lesson 1 SB pages 37 & 38

Trust is one of the most valuable things in our lives, yet it is not always easy to know whom we can rely on. While many people act with honesty and kindness, there are also those who hide their true intentions behind a friendly smile. In life, not everyone we meet is truly honest. Some people put on a friendly face, but are in fact "wolves in sheep's clothing." They may deceive us to gain money, favors, or private information. This can happen anywhere -- at school, in the workplace, or even among people we once considered close friends.

For example, someone might act supportively just to borrow money, with no intention of returning it. Another might spread false stories to damage someone's reputation. Such behavior can leave us feeling betrayed, embarrassed, and unsure whom we can trust.

This type of dishonesty is not limited to face-to-face interactions. In the digital world, fake platforms and social media scams copy these same tactics. They make grand promises—such as free prizes, dream jobs, or fast profits—only to exploit our personal data or disappear with our money. It is like being caught in a trap you did not realise was set.

Whether in daily life or online, there are warning signs:

- The person or platform applies pressure to make you act quickly.
- The story changes when you ask for details.
- The promises seem too good to be true.

To protect yourself, pause before acting, ask careful questions, and confirm.

يتم تكوين السؤال بـ أداة استفهام كالتالي:

| If / When | جملة مضارع بسيط | + | Q.W | + | do / does | + | subj. + inf. | + | ؟ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**أمثلة:**
- If / When we mix red and yellow, what do we get?
- What do we get if / when we mix red and yellow?

#### الاستخدامات Uses

- **التعبير عن الحقائق العامة:**
  - If / When we freeze water, it turns into ice.

- **التعبير عن العادات الثابتة أو المواقف التي لها نتيجة منطقية:**
  - If / When I'm late for work, I take a taxi.
  - If / When I go to bed late, I feel tired the next morning.

- مع الحقيقة التي تخص موقف معين أو محددة بوقت معين يفضل أن نستخدم الحالة الأولى وليس الحالة الصفرية:
  - (حقيقة عامة - حالة صفرية) If you drop glass, it breaks.
  - (موقف محدد - حالة أولى) If you drop this glass, it will break.

- لاحظ أن المضارع البسيط قد يكون مثبت أو منفى:
  - If / When we put water in a freezer, it doesn't turn into steam.

- لاحظ أن المضارع البسيط قد يكون معلوم أو مجهول:
  - If / When water is put in a freezer, it doesn't turn into steam.

### First Conditional

#### Formation
تتكون الحالة الشرطية الأولى من:

- **If / Unless** + جملة مضارع بسيط + **will / won't** + inf.

**أمثلة:**
- If he works hard, he will earn a lot of money.
- = He will earn a lot of money if he works hard.
- = Unless he works hard, he won't earn a lot of money.
- = He won't earn a lot of money unless he works hard.

#### تكوين السؤال بـ «هل»

يتم تكوين السؤال بـ «هل» كالتالي:

- **If / Unless** + جملة مضارع بسيط + **will / won't** + subj. + inf.؟

**أمثلة:**
- If he works hard, will he earn a lot of money?
- Will he earn a lot of money if he works hard?

#### تكوين السؤال بأداة استفهام

يتم تكوين السؤال بـ أداة استفهام كالتالي:

- **If / Unless** + جملة مضارع بسيط + أداة استفهام + **will** + subj. + inf.؟

**أمثلة:**
- If he works hard, what will he earn?
- = What will he earn if he works hard?

#### الاستخدامات

التعبير عن مواقف قابلة للحدوث في المستقبل:

**مثال:**
- If I have enough money, I will buy a car.

يمكن استخدام **(can - may - might - must - should)** بدلاً من **(will)** للتعبير عن القدرة أو الاحتمال أو الضرورة أو النصيحة في المستقبل في جملة جواب الشرط:

**أمثلة:**
- If you feel tired, you should stop the car and take a rest. (نصيحة)
- If I want to come first, I must study hard. (ضرورة)

#### If - In case

- **If** تعني أن الحدث سيقع فقط إذا توفر شرط معين:
  - **مثال:** I'll buy some sandwiches if I feel hungry. (سأشتري فقط إذا شعرت بالجوع)

- بينما تستخدم **in case** بمعنى (في حالة) للدلالة على القيام بشيء تحسبًا للحاجة إليه مستقبلًا:
  - **مثال:** I'll buy some sandwiches in case I feel hungry. (سأشتري في كل الأحوال تحسبًا لأنني قد أشعر بالجوع فيما بعد)

<!-- بداية الصفحة 77 -->
### Important Notes

Use the simple present tense, not the future, in the if-clause after (if):

- ex. If Ahmed (will call - calls) me, I will tell him the truth.

Use the simple present after (if) if the main clause consists of one of the following forms:

1. inf. / don't + inf. / never + inf. (imperative form)

ex. If anyone (finds - found - had found - will find) my mobile, please take it to the manager's office.

- Don't run away if you (will see - see - saw - seen) a dog in the street.

2. Let's + inf.

ex. - Let's go to the cinema if you (will be - are - were - had been) bored.

3. had better ('d better) + inf.

ex. - If mum (has - had - had had - will have) too much housework, you'd better help her.

4. would rather ('d rather) + inf.

ex. - I'd rather revise for tomorrow's exam if I (will want - want - wanted - had wanted) to get high marks.

5. can / could you + inf. (in polite requests)

ex. - If I (will need - need - needed - had needed) money, could you lend me some?

6. It is + adj. + to + inf.

ex. - It is easy to get married if I (will find - find - found - had found) a good flat.

Use (will) + (inf.) in the main clause if the if-clause is one of the following forms:

1. If + subj. + (would like / would love / would prefer)

ex. - If you'd like to travel by plane, I (get - will get - would get - would have got) a ticket for you.

2. If + subj. + (am / is / are + inf. + ing)

ex. - If you're travelling to Aswan next week, I (go - will go - would go - would have gone) with you.

3. If + subj. + have / has + p.p.

ex. - If you have done your homework, I (let - will let - would let - would have let) you go out.

### Second Conditional: الحالة الثانية

#### التكوين Formation

تتكون الحالة الشرطية الثانية من:

$$If / Unless + جملة ماضي بسيط .... would / wouldn't + inf.$$

**أمثلة:**

- If he studied more, he would get better marks.
- He would get better marks if he studied more.
- = He wouldn't get better marks unless he studied more.

يتم تكوين السؤال بـ «هل» كالتالي:

$$If / Unless + جملة ماضي بسيط .... would / wouldn't + subj. + inf. ?$$

**مثال:**

- If he studied more, would he get better marks?

يتم تكوين السؤال بـ أداة استفهام كالتالي:

$$If / Unless + جملة ماضي بسيط .... Q. + would + subj. + inf. .... ?$$

**مثال:**

- If he studied more, what would he get?
- = What would he get if he studied more?

#### استخدامات Uses

تعبر الحالة الثانية عن مواقف غير محتملة الحدوث في المستقبل:

**مثال:**

- I'm extremely overweight. If I lost much weight, I would run in tomorrow's marathon.

في المثال السابق يقول المتحدث أنه زائد جدًا في الوزن، ولو أنه فقد الكثير من الوزن سيشارك في ماراثون الغد، لكن هذا غير منطقي لأنه لا أحد يفقد الكثير من الوزن في يوم واحد.

أما إذا كان الموقف محتملاً فنستخدم الحالة الأولى، لاحظ المثال التالي:

- I'm fit. If I have the chance, I will run in tomorrow's marathon.

**مثال:**

- If people had wings, they would fly like birds.

التعبير عن مواقف تخيلية مستحيلة الحدوث في المضارع أو المستقبل:

#### إعطاء النصيحة بالصيغة (If I were)

**مثال:**

- You should study hard.
- = If I were you, I would study hard.

يمكن استخدام (could - might) بدلاً من (would) للتعبير عن الإمكانية أو الاحتمال أو النصيحة والافتراض:

**مثال:**

- If I were a bird, I could fly high in the sky.

### Important Notes

#### Using "was / were" with Singular Subjects in Imaginary Situations and Advice
- I have much work today. If I **was / were** not busy, I would play football.

#### Verbs That Do Not Change in the Past Simple
The verbs (cut - put - hit - shut - read) do not change when conjugated and are considered past simple if no addition is made to them:
- If he **read** today's newspapers, he (will - **would**) know the latest news.

#### Second Conditional Rules with "had" and "had to"
- (he - she - it) & (I)
- If I **had** a car, I (will drive - **would drive** - would have driven) you to the airport.
- If she **had** to work, she (will look - **would look** - would have looked) for a job as a secretary.

**Rule 1:** If the condition verb is (had + noun), the sentence is second conditional and we choose **would + (inf)**.

**Rule 2:** If the condition verb is (had to + inf), the sentence is second conditional and we choose **would + inf**.

**Rule 3:** If the result clause is (would have + noun), the sentence is second conditional and we choose **past simple**.

**Rule 4:** If the result clause is (would have to + inf), the sentence is second conditional and we choose **past simple**:
- If my son **passed** the exam, he would have a present.
- If Nada **got** late, she would have to take a taxi.

### Remember

#### Third Conditional

**Statement (الجملة الخبرية):**
If + subj. + had + p.p. ..., subj. + would/could/might + have + p.p. ...
- ex. If he had trained hard, he would / could / might have won yesterday's match.
- He would / could / might have won yesterday's match if he had trained hard.

**Yes/No Question (السؤال بـ «هل»):**
Would/Could/Might + subj. + have + p.p. + if + subj. + ... had + p.p. ...?
- ex. If he had trained hard, would he have won yesterday's match?
- Would he have won yesterday's match if he had trained hard?

**(Wh-) Question (السؤال بأداة استفهام):**
Q.W. + would/could/might + subj. + have + p.p. ... + if + subj. + ... had + p.p. ...?
- ex. If he had trained hard, what would he have done?
- What would he have done if he had trained hard?

### General Notes on Conditionals

يمكن استخدام الروابط التالية بدلاً من (if) ويأتي بعدها جملة:

If = as long as = so long as = providing (that) = provided (that)

- If he takes the medicine, he will get better.
- As long as he takes the medicine, he will get better.

يمكن استخدام حروف الجر والظروف التالية بدلاً من (if) ويأتي بعدها (inf. + ing / noun):

If + جملة = with / by / in case of + noun / (inf. + ing)

- If she comes first, she will get a car as a present.
- In case of coming first, she will get a car as a present.
- With your help, I'll succeed. = (If you help me, I'll succeed.)

- If she sleeps early, she will get up early.

يمكن استخدام (unless) بدلاً من (if) مع مراعاة النفي والإثبات حسب المعنى:

يمكن استخدام (without / but for) بدلاً من (unless) ويأتي بعدها (inf. + ing / noun):

- Unless she sleeps early, she won't get up early.
- Unless + جملة = Without / But for + (inf. + ing) / noun

- Unless he has enough money, he won't buy this flat.
- Without (having) enough money, he won't buy this flat.

يمكن استخدام (If it weren't for) بدلاً من (unless) في الحالة الثانية ويأتي بعدها (inf. + ing / noun):

جملة ماضي بسيط + Unless = If it weren't for + (inf. + ing) / noun

- Unless he had enough money, he wouldn't buy this flat.
- If it weren't for (having) enough money, he wouldn't buy this flat.

لاحظ صيغ إعطاء النصيحة:

If I were you, I'd + inf. = You + should / had better / ought to + inf.

- You'd better eat healthy food.
- If I were you, I would eat healthy food.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 81 -->
### استخدام (Should) بدلاً من (If) في الحالتين الشرطية الأولى والثانية

If + subj. + present simple = Should + subj. + inf. ...

- If Hamza helps me, I'll do it well. = Should Hamza help me, I'll do it well.

If + subj. + past simple = Should + subj. + inf. ...

- If Adham had much time, he would help me. = Should Adham have much time, he would help me.

### استخدام (Were) بدلاً من (If) في الحالة الثانية

If + subj. + past simple = Were + subj. + (to + inf.) ...

- If you told me, I would understand. = Were you to tell me, I would understand.

لاحظ أنه إذا كانت (were) فعلًا أساسيًا للجملة لا تستخدم (to + inf.) بعد الفاعل:

- If I were a good footballer, I would be famous. = Were I a good footballer, I would be famous.

### استخدام (Had) بدلاً من (If) في الحالة الثانية عندما تكون فعلًا أساسيًا للشرط

If + subj. + had + ... = Had + subj. + ...

- If I had enough time, I would help you. = Had I enough time, I would help you.

كما يمكن استخدام (Had) بدلاً من (If) في الحالة الشرطية الثالثة:

If + subj. + had + p.p. = Had + subj. + p.p.

- If he had already left, I would have called him. = Had he already left, I would have called him.

### صيغة المفعول لأجله (Causative) في الجمل الشرطية

If + subj. + had + obj. + p.p. (حالة ثانية)

If + subj. + had had + obj. + p.p. (حالة ثالثة)

- If he had his camera repaired, he would lend it to me.
- If he had had his camera repaired, he would have lent it to me.

### استخدام (p.p.) أو صفة بعد (if)

يمكن استخدام (p.p.) أو صفة بعد (if) كما يلي:

if + p.p. / adj. = if + it/this/that/he/she ... + be + p.p. / adj.

- I will buy another fan if needed. = I will buy another fan if that is needed.
- She wouldn't use her mobile at work again if warned. = She wouldn't use her mobile at work again if she was warned.
- I would have helped you if possible. = I would have helped you if it had been possible.

يمكن استخدام (Suppose, Imagine) بدلاً من أداة الشرط (if) ويأتي بعدها جملة شرطية كاملة.

استخدم (Were) بدلاً من (If) إذا جاء بعد فاعل الجملة (to + inf).

استخدم (Were) أو (Had) حسب المعنى بدلاً من (If) إذا لم يكن هناك فعل بعد فاعل الجملة.

### Conditional Sentences: Should, Were, Had, and Other Connectors

#### Using "Should" Instead of "If" with Infinitives
When the verb after **he, she, it** is in the infinitive form, use **Should** instead of **If**.

- **Example:** Mariam **should** be clever, she would answer the question.
  - a. Were
  - b. Had
  - c. **Should**
  - d. If

#### Using "But for," "Without," and "In case of" with (inf. + ing)
Use **But for**, **Without**, or **In case of** when followed by a gerund (inf. + ing).

- **Example:** **But for** having a lot of money, he wouldn't have had such an expensive car.
  - a. If
  - b. Unless
  - c. In case
  - d. **But for**

#### Important Note on Connectors with Gerunds
When a connector is followed by a gerund (inf. + ing), it must be a connector that takes a phrase (not a full clause). This applies when the gerund acts as the subject or describes the subject. In this case, you will find a verb after the gerund.

- **Example:** **In case of** working for six hours a day makes you exhausted, you can take a break in the middle.
  - a. If
  - b. Should
  - c. **In case of**
  - d. Without

- **Example:** **Without** staying up affects my health badly, I will sleep earlier from now on.
  - a. If
  - b. **Without**
  - c. In case of
  - d. Unless

### The War of the New Generation

In the past, wars were fought with soldiers, tanks, and planes. Today, a new kind of war is spreading across the world. It does not use bullets or bombs. Instead, it uses words, lies, half-truths, and rumors. Experts call this the "war of the new generation."

In this kind of war, the goal is not to destroy buildings, but to damage trust. Lies can be used to make people angry, afraid, or confused. A rumor can spread quickly through social media, making millions believe something that is not true. When people no longer know what to believe, it becomes easier to control them.

The victims of these "information attacks" can be individuals, companies, or even whole countries. A false story about a famous person can ruin their career. A rumor about a company can cause customers to stop buying its products.

One dangerous thing about this invisible weapon is how hard it is to fight back. Once a lie is shared online, it can travel faster than the truth. People may share it without checking if it is correct. Some do it because they are angry; others because they find it exciting.

Protecting ourselves from this new kind of war requires awareness. We must think before we believe or share a story. We should ask: "Where did this information come from? Is it supported by facts? Who might benefit from me believing this?"

In the war of the new generation, the most powerful defense is a careful and questioning mind.

### Essay Writing Development Plan

1. An essay has three main parts: an introduction, body paragraphs, and a conclusion.
2. The introduction is the first paragraph of the essay.
3. The introduction presents the topic and the main idea.
4. Start the introduction with a hook, such as a strong question.
5. A hook is an opening sentence that catches the reader's interest.
6. Give some background information to explain the topic briefly.
7. End the introduction with a clear thesis statement.
8. A thesis statement presents the essay's main idea or argument.
9. A body paragraph explains and supports the thesis statement.
10. Start each body paragraph with a topic sentence.
11. A topic sentence introduces the main point of the paragraph.
12. In the first body paragraph, introduce the main idea and give a specific example.
13. In the second body paragraph, introduce and explain the second point.
14. Use supporting details, such as facts, examples, and reasons, to support the main idea.
15. Use transitions to connect ideas between sentences and paragraphs.
16. The conclusion is the final paragraph that summarizes and closes the essay.
17. In the conclusion, restate the thesis using different words.
18. End the essay with a final thought, reflection, or call to action.

### Reading Text

After many years since the Industrial Revolution and the misuse of technology, the large-scale production of machines and automobiles has had harmful effects on the environment. These technologies have mainly caused damage in two ways: through air and water pollution, and through the overuse of natural resources. For this reason, environmental concerns have become a major issue across all industries.

#### Why green?

Green is more than just a color. "Going green" means making changes in the way individuals, organizations, and societies live and work so that their actions are more environmentally friendly. Today, "Go Green" has become a widely used slogan in industry.

#### Green Manufacturing

Green manufacturing refers to producing goods in ways that do not harm the environment and that help preserve natural resources for future generations. The concept of "green manufacturing" can be understood in two ways. First, it means producing environmentally friendly products by using renewable energy and clean technologies. Second, it refers to making the manufacturing process itself greener — reducing pollution and waste by cutting down on resource use, recycling, and reusing materials. ### Grammar Focus: Verb Patterns after Certain Expressions

#### Using "to + infinitive" after "would like, love, prefer, continue"

We use **to + infinitive** (not the **-ing** form) after the following verbs when they are preceded by **would**:

- would + like
- would + love
- would + prefer
- would + continue

**Example:**
- I wouldn't like **to be given** instructions.

#### Important Note about "mind"

This rule does **not** apply to the verb **mind**, which is always followed by the **-ing** form.

**Example:**
- He would not mind **coming** to the meeting.

#### Using "to + infinitive" after "remember" and "forget" as imperatives

The **to + infinitive** form is often used after the verbs **remember** and **forget** when they are used as imperative commands (giving orders or instructions).

**Examples:**
- Before going to bed, remember **to turn** off the light.
- Don't forget **to do** your homework before tomorrow's class.

### The Benefits of Learning a Foreign Language

Moreover, they will understand other cultures better, which promotes respect, tolerance, and a broader worldview. If students practiced speaking regularly, they would improve their confidence, fluency, and ability to express themselves clearly in different situations. Schools that provide language programs encourage students to use these skills in real-life experiences, such as traveling, participating in exchange programs, joining international competitions, or using digital communication tools to connect with peers worldwide.

Some students hesitate to learn another language because they feel it is too difficult or time-consuming. However, if they tried consistently and remained motivated, they would gain not only language skills, but also critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, memory improvement, and new perspectives on the world.

In addition, if students spoke multiple languages, they would have more opportunities for higher education and careers in international companies.

In short, learning a foreign language is not just about grammar and vocabulary. It is a key to becoming a global citizen, expanding personal horizons, and contributing positively to a connected and multicultural world.

My name is Salma, and I speak Arabic, English, and Spanish. I grew up in Cairo, but when I was twelve, my family moved to Spain because of my father's job. ### Listening: Modern Technology and Learning Foreign Languages

Learning any foreign language has become easier thanks to modern technology. In the past, students relied only on textbooks and classroom lessons. Today, digital tools provide many opportunities to practice and improve skills in fun and interactive ways.

One of the most popular methods is using language learning applications. These apps offer short daily lessons, vocabulary games, and much pronunciation practice. Many of them use artificial intelligence to adjust the level of difficulty according to the learner's progress. Some learners spend a little time every day, but they still make great progress.

Another useful tool is online video and audio platforms. By watching movies, listening to songs, or following podcasts in the target language, learners can hear natural pronunciation and improve listening skills. Subtitles and playback options make it simple to understand and repeat. However, only a few students make full use of these options.

Social media and messaging platforms also play a role. Learners can connect with native speakers around the world, exchange messages, and even join live video calls. This creates real communication opportunities without traveling abroad. But some students show little interest in using these chances effectively.

Finally, translation software and online dictionaries help students check meanings quickly and build confidence. When used together, these tools turn technology into a powerful partner for mastering new languages. Even if students have few resources, modern tools can still give them much support to reach success.

### Quantifiers and Subject-Verb Agreement

#### Using "a little" / "a few" vs. "little" / "few"

Use "a little" / "a few" to indicate that something is small in quantity but sufficient, and that its smallness does not cause a problem.

#### Expressions of Time, Price, Speed, Distance, and Amounts of Money

Expressions of time, price, speed, distance, and sums of money are treated as singular.

#### Placement of Articles and Quantifiers

The articles (a, an, the) and quantity expressions such as little, few, some, any, many are used before the adjective that precedes the noun, not between the adjective and the noun.

#### Names of Sciences and Activities Ending in "s"

Names of sciences and activities that end in "s" (such as mathematics, physics) are treated as singular.

#### Subject-Verb Agreement with the Original Subject

Use a singular or plural verb according to the original subject, not necessarily the noun that immediately precedes the blank.

### Reading Text On Lesson 4

#### Ramy's Journey to Liverpool

Ramy had always dreamed of traveling abroad. One summer, he finally flew to Liverpool, England. At first, he was excited, but soon he felt anxious. His biggest difficulty was that he couldn't speak English.

At the airport, he struggled to understand the officer's questions. He only smiled and showed his passport, hoping for the best.

In the city, life became more complicated. When he tried to buy a bus ticket, he couldn't explain himself. People behind him grew impatient and he felt embarrassed.

Later, at a restaurant, he wanted chicken but accidentally received fish.

That night, Ramy decided something important: he must learn English. He downloaded a language app, practiced basic phrases, and wrote down useful words.

The next day, he tried saying, "One ticket, please," and "Chicken, please." To his surprise, people understood him! He felt more confident.

As days passed, Ramy spoke more words, greeted locals, and even asked for directions. People appreciated his efforts and were kind to him.

By the end of his trip, Ramy realized that learning English had turned his journey from a struggle into an enriching adventure.

### An Informal Email

An informal email is a personal message sent to friends, family members, or people you know well. It is written in a relaxed, friendly, and casual style. We use informal emails to share news or talk about our daily lives. We can use them to ask about someone, invite, thank, or apologize. Informal emails are suitable for friends, classmates, relatives, and close people. They are not normally used for business or official communication.

We use simple sentences and everyday words in an informal email. We can use contractions such as "I'm," "don't," "haven't," and "can't." We may sometimes use emojis and friendly expressions.

An informal email usually begins with a friendly greeting. Common greetings include "Hi (name)," and "Hello". The opening may include expressions such as "How are You?" or "What's Up?"

The main message contains the topic, news, invitation, or information. The writer should organize the ideas in clear paragraphs.

The email may end with a friendly closing expression. Common closings include "Take care," "Best wishes," "Love," "Yours," and "See you soon!". The writer puts their name after the closing expression.

"Catch up" means to meet or talk and exchange recent news. "Let me know" means to tell or inform someone. "Long time no see" is used when you have not seen someone for a long time. "Talk to you soon" and "See you soon" are friendly ways to end an email.

An informal email usually includes a greeting, an opening, a main message, a closing, and the writer's name.

#### "Navigating Today's Employment Landscape"

The job market has transformed greatly over the past decade. Traditional methods of finding employment—such as reading a newspaper or walking into offices with a resume in hand—have largely given way to digital platforms and networking strategies.

Today's job seekers must maintain a professional online presence. This means having an updated LinkedIn profile, a polished resume, and sometimes even a personal website showing their skills. Employers often screen candidates online before making contact, so your digital footprint can make or break your chances.

Many positions are filled through personal connections rather than public job postings. Attending industry events, joining professional associations, and maintaining relationships with former colleagues can open doors that traditional applications cannot.

### The Changing Job Market

The days of sending the same generic resume to multiple employers are gone. Successful job hunters modify their applications to each specific role, highlighting relevant experience and using keywords from the job description. This personalized approach increases the chances of getting noticed. Modern interviews often involve multiple rounds, including phone screenings, and video interviews. Some companies even use skills-based assessments or ask candidates to complete sample projects. Being prepared for various interview formats is essential. The job search process can be challenging. It's not uncommon for qualified candidates to apply to dozens of positions before landing the right opportunity. Keeping a positive attitude and learning from each experience is important for long-term success.

### The Use of Articles (A, An, The) and Zero Article

#### Before Names of Languages and School Subjects
- We do not use (a/an/the) before the names of languages: English, French, Arabic, Chinese, Turkish, etc.
- Note: If the word "language" comes after the name of the language, we use (the): the English language, the French language.
- We do not use (a/an/the) before the names of school subjects: mathematics, biology, political science.

#### Before Titles Followed by a Person's Name
- We do not use (the) before titles followed by a person's name.
- ex. King Ramses built a lot of temples. (Not: the king Ramses ...)
- ex. President Sadat was a great politician. (Not: the President Sadat ...)

#### Before the Word "Space" When It Means Outer Space
- We do not use (a/an/the) before the word "space" when it means outer space.
- ex. NASA sends spaceships into space.

#### When We Use (the) Before "Space"
- When we use (the) before the word "space", it means an empty place or an area.
- ex. The space in the class isn't enough for ten more students.

#### Before a Noun Followed by a Number as a Distinguisher
- Do not use (a/an/the) before a noun followed by a number as a distinguisher for it.
- ex. I booked seat 25 in carriage 2. (Not: the seat.../ the carriage...)

### Articles (A, An, The) - Rules and Usage

#### Introduction to Articles
Articles are words that define a noun as specific or unspecific. In English, there are three articles: **a**, **an**, and **the**.

#### The Definite Article "The"
The definite article **the** is used before a noun when the speaker believes that the listener knows exactly which noun is being referred to. It is used with specific nouns that are already known or have been mentioned before.

#### The Indefinite Articles "A" and "An"
The indefinite articles **a** and **an** are used before singular countable nouns when referring to something for the first time or when the noun is not specific.

- **A** is used before words that begin with a consonant sound.
- **An** is used before words that begin with a vowel sound.

#### The Zero Article (No Article)
The zero article is used when no article is needed before a noun. This typically occurs with plural nouns, uncountable nouns, or abstract nouns when referring to them in a general sense.

#### Special Cases and Rules

**1. Nouns Modified by a Phrase or Clause**
When a noun is defined by a phrase or clause that follows it, it usually takes **the** before it, even if the relative pronoun is omitted.

**Examples:**
- The information you asked about was correct.
- The exam they have next week will be very difficult.
- The doctor I told you about.

**2. Unique Nouns**
When referring to something that is unique or one of a kind, **the** is used.

**Examples:**
- The weather in Egypt is generally good throughout the year.
- She is the only girl in the class.
- My sister has a flat on the 2nd floor.

**3. Superlatives**
Superlative forms of adjectives take **the** before them.

**Example:**
- It was the best time of my life.

**4. Musical Instruments**
When referring to playing a musical instrument, **the** is used.

**Example:**
- She plays the piano well.

**5. General Statements with Plural or Uncountable Nouns**
When making general statements about plural or uncountable nouns, no article is used.

**Examples:**
- Technology plays an important role in our life.
- They live in a big house near the beach.

**6. European Countries**
Some countries that begin with a vowel sound but have a consonant sound at the beginning take **a** instead of **an**.

**Example:**
- He visited a European country my uncle lives in.

**7. Ordinal Numbers**
Ordinal numbers (first, second, third, etc.) take **the** before them.

**Example:**
- My sister has a flat on the 2nd floor.

**8. Specific Nouns Already Mentioned**
When a noun has been mentioned before and is now being referred to again, **the** is used.

**Examples:**
- I'd like to buy this great car. The car will cost me 10 million pounds.
- I saw an interesting movie last night.

**9. Nouns Followed by Prepositional Phrases**
When a noun is followed by a prepositional phrase that defines it, **the** is used.

**Example:**
- We had a good time at the beach.

**10. Time Expressions**
Certain time expressions require specific articles.

**Example:**
- My brother had an important exam yesterday but he spent an hour watching TV.

### A Resume (CV)

A resume, or CV, is a formal document used when applying for a job. CV stands for curriculum vitae. A resume summarizes your education, work experience, skills, and achievements. It is usually the first document an employer reads about you. A good resume should make a positive first impression. The purpose of a resume is to help you get a job or opportunity. It shows your qualifications and suitability for a position.

A resume should be short - usually one or two pages. Use clear, simple and professional language. Include only information that is relevant to the job. Organize the information so that it is easy to read. Update your resume regularly.

#### Sections of a Resume

The first section is Personal Information. Personal information includes your full name, phone number, email, and city or country.

The Personal Statement or Objective is a short paragraph about who you are. It also explains what you want to achieve in your career.

The Education section lists your qualifications. Educational qualifications should usually be listed with the most recent first. This section may include dates, degree, institution, and grades.

The Work Experience section includes relevant jobs and internships. It can also include volunteer work and important achievements. Work experience may include dates, job titles, company names, and responsibilities.

The Skills section includes technical and personal skills. Technical skills may include languages and computer programs. Personal skills may include communication, teamwork and leadership.

Additional sections may include certifications, projects, hobbies, and references. These additional sections should be included only when they are relevant.

A well-written resume should be short, clear, accurate, organized, and up to date.

### About the Author

Ernest Hemingway (1899-1961) was an American novelist and journalist, famous for his simple yet powerful style of writing. He loved adventure, travel, and the sea. Hemingway fought in wars, hunted in Africa, and lived in Cuba for many years. He won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1954, and "The Old Man and the Sea" (1952) is considered his masterpiece. It was written in Cuba and is often seen as the story that saved Hemingway's reputation when critics thought he had lost his greatness.

Santiago was an old fisherman, and the sea was his companion. His skin had grown dark and leathery from years beneath the burning sun. His eyes were as clear and bright as the sea itself, full of life and determination.

For eighty-four long days, Santiago had gone out into the Gulf Stream and returned empty-handed. Not a single fish had been caught. In his small Cuban village, whispers began to spread. The younger fishermen, who still had luck, laughed at him quietly. They called him *salao*—the worst kind of unlucky. Yet Santiago carried himself with dignity. He walked proudly with his fishing gear over his shoulder, his back straight, as if luck were something that could never truly defeat a man.

Among all the people of the village, only one remained loyal to him: a boy named Manolin. The boy had fished with Santiago since he was just five years old. Now he was twelve, strong and full of admiration for the old man. He loved Santiago like a grandfather. For forty days, Manolin had fished with him, even when there was no catch. But finally, at his parents' order, he had joined another boat—a luckier boat that brought back fish.

Santiago did not feel weak; he walked with dignity and carried his tools proudly. A young boy named Manolin was his only true friend and loved him like a grandfather. Manolin's parents made him join another boat, but he still came to help Santiago every evening. The boy carried the nets, the harpoon, and folded the sail. Santiago told the boy that fishing was not only about luck but also about skill, patience, and courage.

Santiago lived in a very poor hut with only a bed, a chair, a table, and his fishing tools. He loved baseball very much, and his hero was Joe DiMaggio, who showed courage even when he was in pain. Santiago decided that on the eighty-fifth day he would go far into the sea to catch a big fish. That night he dreamed about lions on the beaches of Africa and believed that his luck would change the next day.

The hut where Santiago lived was small, made of faded palm leaves. Inside, it was almost bare. On the walls hung only two pictures. There was a bed made of newspapers, a single blanket, a wooden table, and one chair. There were no luxuries, no decorations, no treasures—except the tools of a fisherman.

### The Old Man and The Sea

He stabbed and slashed, killing one shark and driving the other away. But each battle cost him strength, and the marlin's body grew smaller, its beauty ruined. As the hours passed, more sharks came. The smell of blood had spread far through the sea. Santiago fought them all, his arms burning, his vision blurring. He killed several but knew he could not stop them forever. By afternoon, the marlin was only half a fish. Its head and backbone remained, but much of its flesh was gone. Santiago leaned against the mast, breathing heavily. "I was beaten," he whispered, "but only by sharks, not by the fish." Still, he did not surrender. Every time a new shark attacked, he stood up and fought. He swung the oar-spear until it splintered, then used the tiller, then even the broken pieces of wood. He was an old man with nothing left but his will.

Night fell again, and Santiago was exhausted beyond words. The marlin was now only a skeleton, stripped of nearly all its meat. But Santiago kept sailing toward home, his spirit unbroken. "I fought for the marlin as long as I could," he said aloud to the stars. "He was too noble to be lost without a fight."

At last, silence returned. No more sharks came. The marlin's skeleton glowed white in the moonlight, its long sword rising like a banner of both triumph and tragedy. Santiago looked at it and felt tears in his eyes. "You were my greatest enemy and my greatest friend," he told the fish. "They destroyed you, but they could not destroy my pride. We fought well." He thought of the boy, and a faint smile touched his lips. "The boy will not let me be alone again," he said. "Tomorrow, he will help me. He must."

Santiago steered the little skiff through the dark waters, his body broken but his spirit still alive. He had lost his catch, but he had not lost his dignity. The sea was quiet again, carrying the old man and the skeleton of the marlin slowly toward the shore.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 205 -->
### Critical Thinking Questions and Suggested Answers

#### How do the sharks symbolize destruction in contrast to the nobility of the marlin?

The sharks symbolize mindless destruction and greed, as they tear away the flesh of the marlin without respect, while the marlin itself represents nobility, strength, and beauty even in death.

#### Why does Hemingway emphasize the endless nature of Santiago's struggle?

Hemingway emphasizes the endless struggle to show that human life is defined by constant challenges, and true strength lies in the will to keep fighting even when defeat seems certain.

#### What does the skeleton of the marlin symbolize in the story?

The skeleton of the marlin symbolizes both triumph and tragedy—it represents Santiago's greatest victory but also the heavy loss caused by forces beyond his control.

#### How does Santiago's refusal to surrender show the theme of human dignity?

Santiago's refusal to surrender, even when he is exhausted, shows that human dignity is preserved not by winning, but by fighting with courage, pride, and endurance until the very end.

#### Why do you think Hemingway contrasts the nobility of the marlin with the greed of the sharks?

Hemingway contrasts them to show the difference between nature's beauty and dignity, represented by the marlin, and the destructive, greedy side of nature, represented by the sharks.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 206 -->
### The Old Man and The Sea: Key Themes and Analysis

#### Santiago's Battle with the Sharks and the Struggle Between Man and Nature

The battle shows that man is constantly challenged by nature's forces, and survival requires courage, endurance, and respect for the natural world.

#### The Lesson of Resilience from Santiago's Refusal to Surrender

The lesson is that resilience is not about never failing, but about continuing to fight and preserve dignity even in the face of certain loss.

#### The Marlin's Skeleton as a Symbol of Victory and Defeat

It represents victory because Santiago caught the greatest fish of his life, but also defeat because the sharks destroyed its flesh and left only bones.

#### Santiago's Relationship with the Marlin

Because he respects the fish as a noble opponent, seeing it as more than prey, and feels a spiritual bond with it.

#### The Loss of the Marlin's Flesh and the Meaning of Santiago's Journey

It shifts the journey from a story of material success to one of inner strength, pride, and the value of struggle itself.

#### Santiago's Determination with Broken Tools and Human Dignity

It shows that dignity comes from perseverance and courage, not from the outcome or the tools one has.

#### Santiago's Pride as Separate from Physical Loss

Because pride is a spiritual quality that cannot be destroyed by material loss, proving that dignity is stronger than defeat.
